body: The Sun and its planetary system developed from material in a cloud of gas and dust. Gravity drew material together. A rotating disk surrounded the growing star. In the disk, small solid particles grew into larger bodies through accumulation and some collisions.

Meteorites preserve material from the early Solar System. Observations of disks around young stars provide another way to investigate how planetary systems form. Planet formation concerns the assembly of a planetary body. The emergence of living systems is a separate question.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: This is a simplified formation model; the detailed history of individual bodies remains under investigation.
purpose: Explain the evidence for a common origin and structure of the Solar System.

revision_history.change: Clarified disk formation and identified evidence for the model
